_meta.constructed_by: manual v4 (full read, 2026-08-14) — independent benchmark for complex scientific-paper extraction, not tailored to any specific method. Covers method evolution, parameter laws, method-phenomenon capture, composition, n-ary relations.

node_types.Method: A named modeling approach/theory/law (not paper title, not generic category)
node_types.Parameter: A physical quantity/constant/coefficient appearing in equations (e.g. μ, I, d, P, τ, g, ρ_s, T, A, ξ, μ_s, b)
node_types.Phenomenon: A physical effect/behavior that methods aim to capture (e.g. nonlocal creep, thin-body strengthening, secondary rheology, segregation, hopper clogging)
node_types.Regime: A flow regime (e.g. quasi-static, dense, gaseous/collisional)

relation_types.improves: A improves B's accuracy/applicability, resolving B's limitation
relation_types.adapts: A adapts B to a new scenario
relation_types.defines: A law/equation defines parameter P (Law text→Parameter)
relation_types.applicable_in: A method is applicable in regime R (Method→Regime)
relation_types.composed_of: Method A is composed of / includes Method B (A⊃B)
relation_types.limited_in: A method fails/limited in regime/phenomenon (Method→Phenomenon/Regime, negative)

difficulty_legend.A: cross-paper: A0=same-paper refs, A1=across 2 papers, A2=across 3+ papers
difficulty_legend.B: rich-topology: B0=flat binary, B1=composition, B2=law-constraint nesting, B3=n-ary(≥3 nodes)
